title: Ivo and the Inheritance
premise: Coral Quintana, an insurance investigator whose photographic memory has quietly unraveled three 'accidental' deaths, is hired to find Ivo Marchetti, a lighthouse keeper's heir who vanished from the coastal town of Bellhaven. When she locates his diary and discovers entries written after his disappearance, Coral realizes Ivo staged his vanishing to expose a family trust that has been funding murders for decades—and that someone inside the investigation is feeding the killer every move she makes. As Coral's own buried identity as a Quintana orphan entwines with the Marchetti inheritance, she must bait the killer using herself as evidence, surviving a final confrontation in the flooded cellar beneath the lighthouse where the truth of both families comes to light. In the end, the trust is dissolved, the killer confesses, and Coral—no longer invisible—chooses the found family she built over the bloodline that never wanted her.
about_author: Juniper Halloran is a former maritime insurance clerk who spent eleven years reading other people's claims before writing her own stories. She lives on the Oregon coast, where the fog does half her plotting for her.

chapters.title: The Claim That Wouldn't Close
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A routine missing-person claim lands on her desk: Ivo Marchetti, last seen at Bellhaven Lighthouse three weeks ago. Her photographic memory flags an inconsistency in the tide logs no one else caught. Emotional beat: restless competence masking loneliness—Coral works best alone, and likes it that way.

chapters.title: Bellhaven in Fog
chapters.summary: Coral arrives in town and interviews the tight-knit circle around Ivo: his half-sister Odile, the estate lawyer Prentiss, and harbor master Dee Okonkwo. Everyone is polite; everyone is lying about something small. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: the ache of watching a town that functions as a family she never had.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, One Signature
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter to Coral's earlier cases—the drowned fisherman, the garage carbon monoxide death, the fall from the cliff path—each ruled accidental, each quietly solved by her. POV: Coral, interwoven with a cold-case file excerpt. Emotional beat: vindication soured by the knowledge that no one ever thanked her.

chapters.title: The Diary's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Searching Ivo's cottage, Coral finds his diary. The final dated entry describes his own disappearance in third person—as if he knew he'd vanish. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: first true fear; this isn't a runaway, it's a performance with an audience of one killer.

chapters.title: Odile's Grief, Carefully Worn
chapters.summary: Coral interviews Odile Marchetti again and notices grief performed like a rehearsed monologue—but also genuine tremors when the trust is mentioned. POV: alternating Coral and Odile. Emotional beat: two women recognizing each other as performers, neither sure which of them is acting.

chapters.title: What the Tide Took Back
chapters.summary: A storm washes up Ivo's coat, torn and salt-stiff, near a sea cave. Inside: a key stamped with the Marchetti crest. POV: Coral, with Dee providing local knowledge. Emotional beat: dread deepening into resolve; the case has teeth now.

chapters.title: The Trust Nobody Reads
chapters.summary: Coral pulls the Marchetti family trust documents and discovers a clause paying out on deaths 'by misadventure'—the same phrasing across all three of her old cases. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: cold fury; her quiet victories were never accidents, they were installments.

chapters.title: Someone Is Reading Over My Shoulder
chapters.summary: Coral's confidential notes appear, paraphrased, in an anonymous letter warning her off. Someone inside the investigation—or the firm—is leaking. POV: Coral, paranoid and precise. Emotional beat: isolation sharpening; the invisibility she cultivated has become a liability.

chapters.title: Dee Knows More Than the Harbor
chapters.summary: Harbor master Dee admits she saw a boat the night Ivo vanished and stayed silent to protect someone. POV: Dee, then Coral. Emotional beat: the first crack of alliance—found family beginning to form in unlikely ballast.

chapters.title: Pages After the End
chapters.summary: Coral finds diary pages hidden in the lighthouse—entries continuing past the disappearance date, in Ivo's hand, describing someone watching him write them. He's alive, or was very recently. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: electric hope colliding with terror; the hunter realizes she's also being hunted.

chapters.title: Prentiss's Perfect Alibi
chapters.summary: The estate lawyer produces an airtight alibi for the night of the disappearance—too perfect, memorized like testimony. Coral's memory cross-references a detail he couldn't know unless he'd read the police file. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by doubt; knowing isn't proving.

chapters.title: The Name Quintana
chapters.summary: Digging into the trust's founding, Coral discovers her own surname among the original beneficiaries—an orphaned child signed away decades ago. She may be family. POV: Coral, raw and unguarded. Emotional beat: identity crisis; the case just became personal in the cruelest way.

chapters.title: Midnight at the Salt House
chapters.summary: Coral and Dee break into the derelict Salt House and find financial ledgers linking payments to all three old deaths. They're interrupted; someone torches the boathouse behind them. POV: alternating Coral and Dee. Emotional beat: loyalty forged in fire—literally.

chapters.title: The Trap That Was Set for Me
chapters.summary: Coral realizes the leaked notes weren't carelessness—they were bait, meant to draw her to Bellhaven all along. The killer wanted an investigator with her particular memory. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: vertigo; she stops hunting and starts asking why she was chosen.

chapters.title: Ivo, Alive and Afraid
chapters.summary: Following the diary's coded references, Coral finds Ivo hiding in the sea cave network—emaciated, terrified, unwilling to surface because surfacing means dying. POV: Ivo, then Coral. Emotional beat: relief curdling into shared desperation; two witnesses, one exit.

chapters.title: What Ivo Saw
chapters.summary: Ivo recounts the night of his disappearance: he faked it after finding the trust's murder ledger, but his watcher found the cave entrance days ago. Someone knows exactly where they are. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: guilt and gratitude braided together—he used Coral as a decoy without meaning to.

chapters.title: The Leak Has a Face
chapters.summary: Coral sets a false detail through three different channels—a classic canary trap. The poisoned version surfaces in an anonymous note, exposing the leak: not Prentiss, but the firm's own regional adjuster, Marcus Vane. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: betrayal and clarity arriving in the same breath.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Hours of Fog
chapters.summary: Vane, cornered, moves to destroy the cave evidence before the tide turns—with Ivo still inside. Coral must choose between securing the ledger copy and saving Ivo. POV: alternating Coral and Ivo. Emotional beat: love against duty made literal; she chooses the person, and trusts Dee to hold the proof.

chapters.title: The Flooded Cellar
chapters.summary: Climax. Beneath the lighthouse, Coral confronts Vane in the rising water of the old cellar, trading her photographic testimony against his confession while Ivo records everything. Vane nearly drowns her; Dee and the sheriff arrive at the last moment. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into fierce, visible courage.

chapters.title: Confession in Ink
chapters.summary: Vane confesses to three murders and the attempt on Ivo, implicating the trust's silent trustees. The diary, the ledgers, and Coral's memory form an unbreakable record. POV: Coral, with transcript excerpts. Emotional beat: exhausted justice; the invisible woman becomes the record itself.

chapters.title: What Inheritance Means
chapters.summary: The trust is dissolved. Coral learns she was named a beneficiary as a child—then signs her share over to fund Bellhaven's harbor school, severing the bloodline tie on her own terms. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: grief and release; identity chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: Visible
chapters.summary: Epilogue. Months later, Coral stays in Bellhaven—not as an investigator but as herself, Sunday dinners at Dee's table, Ivo restoring the lighthouse lamp. A new case file arrives; she reads it slowly, unhurried, surrounded. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: quiet joy; staying invisible was never really an option, and she no longer wants it to be.
